name: Maqam Hijaz
description: Characterized by an augmented second interval, creating a distinctive and dramatic sound.

name: Maqam Rast
description: The foundational Maqam, often compared to the Western major scale but with neutral thirds.

name: Maqam Bayati
description: Features a neutral second and is known for its soulful and melancholic character.

name: Maqam Saba
description: A highly emotional Maqam with unstable intervals and a unique descending character.

name: Maqam Nahawand
description: Similar to the Western minor scale, often used for romantic or grand themes.

name: Maqam Kurd
description: Based on the Phrygian mode, it evokes a sense of folk-like simplicity and earthiness.

name: Dastgah-e Shur
description: Considered the 'mother of Persian modes', it is deeply expressive and widely used.

name: Turkish Hicaz
description: The Turkish variant of Hijaz, used in both classical and popular Ottoman music.

name: Maqam Ajam
description: Equivalent to the Western major scale, conveying joy, strength, and clarity.

name: Mugam Segah
description: An Azeri mode with a focus on the neutral third, central to Mugam traditions.

name: Andalusian Nubah
description: A suite form from Moorish Spain, with complex rhythmic cycles and modal evolution.

name: Iraqi Maqam
description: A specific repertoire and performance practice of Maqam in Baghdad, highly refined.

name: Raga Yaman
description: A heptatonic scale corresponding to the Lydian mode, often performed in the evening.

name: Raga Bhairav
description: A morning Raga with flat second and sixth degrees, evoking seriousness and devotion.

name: Raga Todi
description: A morning Raga expressing gentle pathos and longing, with flat 2nd, 3rd, and 6th.

name: Raga Malkauns
description: A late-night pentatonic Raga with a powerful, meditative, and introspective mood.

name: Raga Darbari
description: A grave, late-night Raga known for its deep, oscillating notes and profound mood.

name: Carnatic Mayamalavagowla
description: The fundamental scale for beginners in Carnatic music, similar to Bhairav.

name: Raga Bhimpalasi
description: An afternoon Raga with a pentatonic ascent and heptatonic descent, expresses longing.

name: Raga Bageshri
description: A late-night Raga conveying the pain of separation and the wait for a lover.

name: Carnatic Shankarabharanam
description: Equivalent to the Western major scale, a parent scale for many ragas.

name: Qawwali Music
description: Sufi devotional music with strong vocal performances and driving rhythms.

name: Pentatonic Chinese (Gong)
description: A foundational anhemitonic (no semitones) pentatonic scale associated with the earth element.

name: Japanese In-Sen Scale
description: A pentatonic scale with characteristic half steps, used for koto and shamisen music.

name: Javanese Gamelan Slendro
description: A pentatonic scale with nearly equidistant intervals, a core tuning of Gamelan music.

name: Javanese Gamelan Pelog
description: A heptatonic scale with large and small intervals, from which pentatonic subsets are chosen.

name: Korean Pyeongjo Mode
description: A pentatonic mode often used in folk music, conveying a bright and peaceful mood.

name: Vietnamese Hue Style
description: Music of the imperial court, featuring unique microtonal inflections and ornamentation.

name: Japanese Gagaku Ryo
description: A scale from ancient court music, similar to the Lydian mode, creating a feeling of suspension.

name: Mongolian Long Song
description: Characterized by wide vocal ranges and free rhythm, based on pentatonic scales.

name: Thai Classical Scale
description: A seven-note equidistant scale, where each step is approximately 171 cents.

name: Balinese Gamelan
description: Known for its shimmering, fast-paced, and rhythmically complex interlocking patterns.

name: Gregorian Mode 1 (Dorian)
description: A diatonic mode with a characteristic minor sixth, used extensively in early sacred chant.

name: Phrygian Dominant
description: Also known as Spanish Gypsy scale, it is a hallmark of Flamenco music.

name: Celtic Air (Aeolian)
description: The natural minor scale, common in ballads and slow airs, evoking melancholy.

name: Byzantine Chromatic
description: A scale used in Greek Orthodox chant, with two augmented second intervals.

name: Hungarian Minor Scale
description: A harmonic minor scale with a raised fourth, giving it a distinctive character.

name: Swedish Lydian-Dominant
description: A Lydian scale with a flat 7th, common in Nordic folk music, especially polskas.

name: Russian Minor (Gypsy)
description: A scale with a minor third and sixth but major second and seventh, very dramatic.

name: Alpine Yodel Mode
description: Often based on major pentatonic scales to facilitate large vocal leaps.

name: West African Pentatonic
description: A common pentatonic scale used by instruments like the Kora and Balafon.

name: Ethiopian Ambasel Scale
description: A pentatonic scale with a unique intervallic structure, used in traditional ballads.

name: Mbira Music (Shona)
description: Complex polyrhythmic music based on a heptatonic scale with a distinctive tuning.

name: Ewe Music (Ghana)
description: Focuses on complex drum ensembles and bell patterns, often with a heptatonic modal feel.

name: Mande Balafon Scale
description: An equidistant heptatonic scale used for the balafon, a gourd-resonated xylophone.

name: Gnawa Music (Morocco)
description: Ritual trance music based on pentatonic scales, played on the guembri and qraqeb.

name: Wassoulou Music (Mali)
description: A popular music genre based on a pentatonic scale, driven by strong female vocalists.

name: Afro-Cuban Clave Rhythm
description: While primarily rhythmic, melodies often use pentatonic or hexatonic scales.
